title: The 7th Guest historical rare B-picture failures
symptom: The original full five-play VMPEG run accumulated five rejected pictures; two captured failures followed a runtime elementary-stream divergence during the branched third play
expected: The native CDIC/PCL/VMPEG path delivers complete MPEG pictures across repeated plays without decoder errors or a title-specific recovery path

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: The rejected pictures were incomplete because the old separately modeled CDIC/VMPEG interrupt paths allowed native PCL ownership to be reordered and runtime elementary delivery to diverge from the complete on-disc stream.
supporting_evidence: The historical runtime capture matched the contiguous extraction for 1,017,394 bytes before diverging.
The two captured B pictures rejected midway through macroblock parsing while the contiguous stream decoded.
The later shared-IN4 investigation proved that VMPEG could preempt the active CDIC handler before its PCL producer-pointer update, leading to reuse of that PCL.
contradicting_evidence: The original failure trace did not independently identify the exact missing byte boundary for every one of the five rejected pictures.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Repeat the full five-play scenario after shared-IN4 arbitration while preserving cumulative decoder-error accounting; any deterministic rejection would show that interrupt arbitration was insufficient.
citations: Philips CD-i 220 service manual section 6.6.1 and signal glossary

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: An abort/restart or seamless branch retained an invalid delayed-reference pair, causing otherwise complete B pictures to fail.
supporting_evidence: Philips TN 088 documents stale B-pictures after abort/restart.
Two historical failures occurred in a branched play.
contradicting_evidence: Stale reference pixels can corrupt prediction output but do not explain failure to parse a variable-length code midway through a macroblock.
The current decoder logic is materially unchanged and now parses the complete five-play run without error.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Decode the same complete coded picture with fresh and deliberately stale reference pixels; identical parse completion with different pixels falsifies stale references as the cause of a VLC rejection.

context.scenario: five-play The 7th Guest Europe Disc 1 run with one scripted title-menu click

experiments.strategy: Run the exact current bounded scenario twice with cumulative DVC diagnostics, then compare every retained event and the final machine, framebuffer, and audio hashes. Do not change decoder behavior.
assumptions: Five observed VMPEG play events cover the repeated-play class in which the original errors accumulated.
The cumulative video-error counter remains preserved across transport and decoder resets.
experiments.expected: If the shared-IN4 prerequisite superseded the old transport failure, both runs finish with identical evidence and zero cumulative decoder errors.
experiments.actual: Both 1.1-billion-instruction runs were identical: five VMPEG plays, 16,619 packs, 7,853 decoded and presented video frames, 25,226 decoded audio frames, matching machine/framebuffer/audio hashes, and zero demux, video, audio, or stream errors. The diagnostic comparator found no divergence.
improvements: The historical M3.13 blocker is removed without concealment, smoothing, or title-specific decoder behavior.
The next work is isolated TN 088 transition compliance rather than recovery for an obsolete live-stream phenotype.
experiments.evidence_quality: high: two exact deterministic full runs, cumulative reset-safe counters, and retained historical transport evidence

conditions: CD-i 220/Mono-I with VMPEG and the shared-IN4 daisy-chain model.
The recorded disc fingerprint and five-play scripted scenario.
invalidated_by: Changes to CDIC/VMPEG shared-IN4 arbitration, PCL ownership, DMA2 transport, decoder reset, or cumulative error accounting.
repeat_when: A current build reports a decoder error in a repeated or branched VMPEG play.

manual_verification.notes: Two exact headless full runs and their final hashes/counters match. No additional manual visual check is required to close the obsolete decoder-error count; separate visual transition incidents remain open.
